sanskrit: anasūyā kṣamā śāntiḥ saṃtoṣaḥ priyavāditā satyaṃ dānam anāyāso naiṣa mārgo durātmanām
english: Freedom from envy, patience, tranquillity, contentment, gentle speech, truthfulness, charity, and freedom from restlessness — this is not the path of the wicked of soul.

sanskrit: kāmakrodhau vaśe kṛtvā brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ vikramya ghore tapasi brāhmaṇaḥ saṃśitavrataḥ kālākāṅkṣī carel lokān nirapāya ivātmavān
english: Having mastered desire and anger, chaste and conquering his senses, the brāhmaṇa of stern vows, striving valiantly in dread austerity and awaiting his hour, should walk the worlds self-possessed, as one beyond all harm.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dvijātayo vratopetā yad idaṃ bhuñjate haviḥ annaṃ brāhmaṇakāmāya katham etat pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When the twice-born, devoted to their vows, eat this oblation, this food intended for the brāhmaṇas — how is that, grandfather?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca avedoktavratopetā bhuñjānāḥ kāryakāriṇaḥ vedokteṣu ca bhuñjānā vrataluptā yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: Those who, observing vows not enjoined by the Veda, eat thus are merely doers of deeds; and those who eat while bound by vows the Veda enjoins are breakers of their vows, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yad idaṃ tapa ity āhur upavāsaṃ pṛthagjanāḥ etat tapo mahārāja utāho kiṃ tapo bhavet
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: That which the common folk call austerity — namely fasting — is this austerity, O great king, or what truly may austerity be?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca māsapakṣopavāsena manyante yat tapo janāḥ ātmatantropaghātaḥ sa na tapas tat satāṃ matam tyāgaś ca sannatiś caiva śiṣyate tapa uttamam
english: Bhīṣma said: That which people deem austerity — fasting for a month or a fortnight — is but the ruin of one's own self-discipline; it is not austerity, so the good hold. Renunciation and humility — these are taught to be the highest austerity.

sanskrit: sadopavāsī ca bhaved brahmacārī sadaiva ca muniś ca syāt sadā vipro daivataṃ ca sadā bhajet
english: One should ever be a faster and ever a celibate; the wise man should ever be a sage and should ever worship the deity.

sanskrit: kuṭumbiko dharmakāmaḥ sadāsvapnaś ca bhārata amāṃsāśī sadā ca syāt pavitraṃ ca sadā japet
english: A householder devoted to dharma, ever wakeful, O Bhārata, should ever abstain from flesh and should ever recite the sacred texts.

sanskrit: amṛtāśī sadā ca syān na ca syād viṣabhojanaḥ vighasāśī sadā ca syāt sadā caivātithipriyaḥ
english: He should ever eat what is like nectar and never feed on what is like poison; he should ever be one who eats the leavings of the offering, and ever cherish his guests.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ sadopavāsī syād brahmacārī kathaṃ bhavet vighasāśī kathaṃ ca syāt sadā caivātithipriyaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How is one ever a faster, how a celibate, how an eater of the offering's leavings, and how ever a cherisher of guests?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca antarā prātarāśaṃ ca sāyamāśaṃ tathaiva ca sadopavāsī ca bhaved yo na bhuṅkte kathaṃ cana
english: Bhīṣma said: He who never eats anything at all between the morning meal and the evening meal — he is the perpetual faster.

sanskrit: bhāryāṃ gacchan brahmacārī ṛtau bhavati brāhmaṇaḥ ṛtavādī sadā ca syāj jñānanityaś ca yo naraḥ
english: The brāhmaṇa who approaches his wife only in her season is a celibate; and that man is so who is ever truthful in speech and ever devoted to knowledge.

sanskrit: abhakṣayan vṛthāmāṃsam amāṃsāśī bhavaty uta dānanityaḥ pavitraś ca asvapnaś ca divāsvapan
english: He who does not eat flesh taken in vain becomes an abstainer from flesh; ever charitable and pure, and wakeful even though he sleep by day.

sanskrit: bhṛtyātithiṣu yo bhuṅkte bhuktavatsu sadā sa ha amṛtaṃ sakalaṃ bhuṅkta iti viddhi yudhiṣṭhira
english: He who eats only after his dependants and guests have eaten — know, Yudhiṣṭhira, that such a one wholly partakes of nectar.

sanskrit: abhuktavatsu nāśnānaḥ satataṃ yas tu vai dvijaḥ abhojanena tenāsya jitaḥ svargo bhavaty uta
english: That twice-born one who never eats until others have eaten — by such abstention is heaven won by him.

sanskrit: devatābhyaḥ pitṛbhyaś ca bhṛtyebhyo 'tithibhiḥ saha avaśiṣṭaṃ tu yo 'śnāti tam āhur vighasāśinam
english: He who eats only what remains after the gods, the ancestors, the dependants, and the guests have been served — him they call an eater of the leavings of the offering.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ lokā hy aparyantāḥ sadane brahmaṇā saha upasthitāś cāpsarobhiḥ pariyānti divaukasaḥ
english: For such men there are worlds without end in the abode of Brahmā; attended by apsarases, they move about as dwellers of heaven.

sanskrit: devatābhiś ca ye sārdhaṃ pitṛbhiś copabhuñjate ramante putrapautraiś ca teṣāṃ gatir anuttamā
english: Those who partake of food together with the gods and the ancestors, and who delight in their sons and grandsons — theirs is the most surpassing destiny.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yad idaṃ karma loke 'smiñ śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham puruṣaṃ yojayaty eva phalayogena bhārata
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Whatever deed is done in this world, whether good or evil, surely binds a man to the yoking of its fruit, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kartā svit tasya puruṣa utāho neti saṃśayaḥ etad icchāmi tattvena tvattaḥ śrotuṃ pitāmaha
english: Is man indeed the doer of that deed, or is he not? — such is my doubt. This I wish to hear from you in its truth, grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam prahrādasya ca saṃvādam indrasya ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: On this point too they recount an ancient tale, the dialogue between Prahrāda and Indra, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: asaktaṃ dhūtapāpmānaṃ kule jātaṃ bahuśrutam astambham anahaṃkāraṃ sattvasthaṃ samaye ratam
english: Unattached, his sins shaken off, nobly born and deeply learned, free of rigidity, free of self-conceit, established in goodness, devoted to right conduct —

sanskrit: tulyanindāstutiṃ dāntaṃ śūnyāgāraniveśanam carācarāṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ viditaprabhavāpyayam
english: holding blame and praise alike, self-controlled, dwelling in an empty house, knowing the rising and the passing-away of beings both moving and unmoving —

sanskrit: akrudhyantam ahṛṣyantam apriyeṣu priyeṣu ca kāñcane vātha loṣṭe vā ubhayoḥ samadarśanam
english: never angered, never elated amid things unwelcome or welcome, looking with an even eye on both gold and a clod of earth —

sanskrit: ātmaniḥśreyasajñāne dhīraṃ niścitaniścayam parāvarajñaṃ bhūtānāṃ sarvajñaṃ samadarśanam
english: steadfast in the knowledge of the soul's highest good, firm in resolve, knowing the higher and lower of beings, all-knowing, looking on all alike —

sanskrit: śakraḥ prahrādam āsīnam ekānte saṃyatendriyam bubhutsamānas tat prajñām abhigamyedam abravīt
english: Śakra, desiring to understand that wisdom of his, approached Prahrāda — seated apart, his senses restrained — and spoke thus.

sanskrit: yaiḥ kaiś cit saṃmato loke guṇaiḥ syāt puruṣo nṛṣu bhavaty anapagān sarvāṃs tān guṇāṃl lakṣayāmahe
english: Whatever qualities make a man esteemed among men in this world — all those qualities, never departed from you, do we observe in you.

sanskrit: atha te lakṣyate buddhiḥ samā bālajanair iha ātmānaṃ manyamānaḥ sañ śreyaḥ kim iha manyase
english: And yet your mind seems here level with that of the simple folk. Regarding yourself as you do, what do you hold to be the good in this world?

sanskrit: baddhaḥ pāśaiś cyutaḥ sthānād dviṣatāṃ vaśam āgataḥ śriyā vihīnaḥ prahrāda śocitavye na śocasi
english: Bound in fetters, fallen from your station, brought under the power of your foes, bereft of fortune — Prahrāda, in a plight to be mourned, you do not mourn.

sanskrit: prajñālābhāt tu daiteya utāho dhṛtimattayā prahrāda svastharūpo 'si paśyan vyasanam ātmanaḥ
english: Is it through the attainment of wisdom, O Daitya, or through firmness of resolve, that you remain serene in form, Prahrāda, even as you behold your own calamity?

sanskrit: iti saṃcoditas tena dhīro niścitaniścayaḥ uvāca ślakṣṇayā vācā svāṃ prajñām anuvarṇayan
english: Thus urged by him, the steadfast one, firm in his resolve, spoke in gentle words, setting forth his own wisdom.

sanskrit: pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca bhūtānāṃ yo na budhyate tasya stambho bhaved bālyān nāsti stambho 'nupaśyataḥ
english: He who does not understand the arising and the ceasing of beings — in him there is rigidity born of folly; but for one who perceives truly there is no rigidity.

sanskrit: svabhāvāt saṃpravartante nivartante tathaiva ca sarve bhāvās tathābhāvāḥ puruṣārtho na vidyate
english: From their own nature all states of being arise and likewise cease, both the existent and the non-existent; human effort has no place therein.

sanskrit: puruṣārthasya cābhāve nāsti kaś cit svakārakaḥ svayaṃ tu kurvatas tasya jātu māno bhaved iha
english: And in the absence of human effort there is no agent of one's own; but for him who fancies he acts of himself, conceit may sometimes arise here.

sanskrit: yas tu kartāram ātmānaṃ manyate sādhvasādhunoḥ tasya doṣavatī prajñā svamūrtyajñeti me matiḥ
english: He who deems himself the doer of good and of ill — his wisdom is flawed, ignorant of its own true form: such is my judgement.

sanskrit: yadi syāt puruṣaḥ kartā śakrātmaśreyase dhruvam ārambhās tasya sidhyeran na ca jātu parābhavet
english: If man were truly the doer for his own welfare, O Śakra, then surely his undertakings would all succeed, and he would never meet defeat.

sanskrit: aniṣṭasya hi nirvṛttir anivṛttiḥ priyasya ca lakṣyate yatamānānāṃ puruṣārthas tataḥ kutaḥ
english: For even among those who strive, the coming-to-pass of the undesired and the not-coming-to-pass of the dear is seen; whence, then, is human effort efficacious?

sanskrit: aniṣṭasyābhinirvṛttim iṣṭasaṃvṛttim eva ca aprayatnena paśyāmaḥ keṣāṃ cit tat svabhāvataḥ
english: We see, for some men, the coming-about of the undesired and the gaining of the desired without any effort at all — that comes of their nature.

sanskrit: pratirūpadharāḥ ke cid dṛśyante buddhisattamāḥ virūpebhyo 'lpabuddhibhyo lipsamānā dhanāgamam
english: Some comely of form and most excellent in intellect are seen craving the gain of wealth from men ill-formed and of little intellect.

sanskrit: svabhāvapreritāḥ sarve niviśante guṇā yadā śubhāśubhās tadā tatra tasya kiṃ mānakāraṇam
english: When all the qualities, fair and foul, settle upon a man, driven by his own nature — then what cause is there for his pride therein?

sanskrit: svabhāvād eva tat sarvam iti me niścitā matiḥ ātmapratiṣṭhitā prajñā mama nāsti tato 'nyathā
english: All this proceeds from nature alone — such is my settled conviction. My wisdom rests within the self; for me there is nothing otherwise.

sanskrit: karmajaṃ tv iha manye 'haṃ phalayogaṃ śubhāśubham karmaṇāṃ viṣayaṃ kṛtsnam ahaṃ vakṣyāmi tac chṛṇu
english: Yet here I hold the yoking of fruit, fair or foul, to be born of deeds; the whole domain of deeds I shall declare — hear it.

sanskrit: yathā vedayate kaś cid odanaṃ vāyaso vadan evaṃ sarvāṇi karmāṇi svabhāvasyaiva lakṣaṇam
english: As a crow by its cawing makes known its boiled rice, even so are all deeds but the mark of one's own nature.

sanskrit: vikārān eva yo veda na veda prakṛtiṃ parām tasya stambho bhaved bālyān nāsti stambho 'nupaśyataḥ
english: He who knows only the modifications and knows not the supreme primal nature — in him there is rigidity born of folly; but for one who perceives truly there is no rigidity.

sanskrit: svabhāvabhāvino bhāvān sarvān eveha niścaye budhyamānasya darpo vā māno vā kiṃ kariṣyati
english: For one who, in firm conviction, understands that all states of being arise here from nature — what can arrogance or conceit do to him?

sanskrit: veda dharmavidhiṃ kṛtsnaṃ bhūtānāṃ cāpy anityatām tasmāc chakra na śocāmi sarvaṃ hy evedam antavat
english: I know the whole ordinance of dharma and the impermanence of beings; therefore, O Śakra, I do not grieve, for all this is bound to come to an end.

sanskrit: nirmamo nirahaṃkāro nirīho muktabandhanaḥ svastho 'vyapetaḥ paśyāmi bhūtānāṃ prabhavāpyayau
english: Free of mine-ness, free of self-conceit, free of craving, released from bondage, serene and undeparted from myself, I behold the rising and the passing-away of beings.

sanskrit: kṛtaprajñasya dāntasya vitṛṣṇasya nirāśiṣaḥ nāyāso vidyate śakra paśyato lokavidyayā
english: For one whose wisdom is perfected, who is self-controlled, free of thirst and free of craving, who sees through the knowledge of the world — no toil of mind remains, O Śakra.

sanskrit: prakṛtau ca vikāre ca na me prītir na ca dviṣe dveṣṭāraṃ na ca paśyāmi yo mamādya mamāyate
english: In primal nature and in its modifications I have neither attachment nor aversion; nor do I see any foe who today claims me as his own.

sanskrit: nordhvaṃ nāvāṅ na tiryak ca na kva cic chakra kāmaye na vijñāne na vijñeye nājñāne śarma vidyate
english: Not above, not below, not athwart, nor anywhere, O Śakra, do I desire aught; neither in knowing, nor in the knowable, nor in not-knowing is any refuge found.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca yenaiṣā labhyate prajñā yena śāntir avāpyate prabrūhi tam upāyaṃ me samyak prahrāda pṛcchate
english: Śakra said: By what is this wisdom won, by what is peace attained? Declare to me that means, Prahrāda, rightly, as I ask.

sanskrit: prahrāda uvāca ārjavenāpramādena prasādenātmavattayā vṛddhaśuśrūṣayā śakra puruṣo labhate mahat
english: Prahrāda said: By uprightness, by vigilance, by serenity, by self-possession, and by service to the elders, O Śakra, a man attains the great.

sanskrit: svabhāvāl labhate prajñāṃ śāntim eti svabhāvataḥ svabhāvād eva tat sarvaṃ yat kiṃ cid anupaśyasi
english: From nature he gains wisdom, by nature he comes to peace; from nature alone is all that whatsoever you behold.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity ukto daityapatinā śakro vismayam āgamat prītimāṃś ca tadā rājaṃs tad vākyaṃ pratyapūjayat
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed by the lord of the Daityas, Śakra fell to wonder; and well-pleased then, O king, he honoured those words.

sanskrit: sa tadābhyarcya daityendraṃ trailokyapatir īśvaraḥ asurendram upāmantrya jagāma svaṃ niveśanam
english: Then the sovereign lord of the three worlds, having honoured the Daitya chief, took leave of the lord of the Asuras and departed to his own abode.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yayā buddhyā mahīpālo bhraṣṭaśrīr vicaren mahīm kāladaṇḍaviniṣpiṣṭas tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: With what understanding should a king, fallen from his fortune, crushed by the rod of Time, wander over the earth? Tell me that, grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam vāsavasya ca saṃvādaṃ baler vairocanasya ca
english: Bhīṣma said: On this point too they recount an ancient tale, the dialogue between Vāsava and Bali, the son of Virocana.

sanskrit: pitāmaham upāgatya praṇipatya kṛtāñjaliḥ sarvān evāsurāñ jitvā baliṃ papraccha vāsavaḥ
english: Having conquered all the Asuras, Vāsava approached the Grandsire, bowed down with hands joined in reverence, and asked about Bali.

sanskrit: yasya sma dadato vittaṃ na kadā cana hīyate taṃ baliṃ nādhigacchāmi brahmann ācakṣva me balim
english: He whose wealth, however much he gave, was never once diminished — that Bali I cannot find. O Brahmā, tell me where Bali is.

sanskrit: sa eva hy astam ayate sa sma vidyotate diśaḥ sa varṣati sma varṣāṇi yathākālam atandritaḥ taṃ baliṃ nādhigacchāmi brahmann ācakṣva me balim
english: It was he who set as the sun, he who illumined the quarters, he who, unwearying, poured down the rains in their season. That Bali I cannot find. O Brahmā, tell me where Bali is.

sanskrit: sa vāyur varuṇaś caiva sa raviḥ sa ca candramāḥ so 'gnis tapati bhūtāni pṛthivī ca bhavaty uta taṃ baliṃ nādhigacchāmi brahmann ācakṣva me balim
english: He was the Wind and Varuṇa, he the Sun and the Moon; he was Agni who warms all beings, and he the very Earth. That Bali I cannot find. O Brahmā, tell me where Bali is.

sanskrit: brahmovāca naitat te sādhu maghavan yad etad anupṛcchasi pṛṣṭas tu nānṛtaṃ brūyāt tasmād vakṣyāmi te balim
english: Brahmā said: This is not seemly in you, O Maghavan, that you ask this; yet one questioned should not utter falsehood — therefore I shall tell you of Bali.

sanskrit: uṣṭreṣu yadi vā goṣu khareṣv aśveṣu vā punaḥ variṣṭho bhavitā jantuḥ śūnyāgāre śacīpate
english: Among camels, or among cattle, among asses, or again among horses, that creature shall come to dwell, the best of his kind, in an empty house, O lord of Śacī.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca yadi sma balinā brahmañ śūnyāgāre sameyivān hanyām enaṃ na vā hanyāṃ tad brahmann anuśādhi mām
english: Śakra said: If, O Brahmā, I should meet with Bali in that empty house, should I slay him or not slay him? Instruct me in this, O Brahmā.

sanskrit: brahmovāca mā sma śakra baliṃ hiṃsīr na balir vadham arhati nyāyāṃs tu śakra praṣṭavyas tvayā vāsava kāmyayā
english: Brahmā said: Do not, O Śakra, harm Bali; Bali does not deserve to be killed. Yet you may, Vāsava, question him on points of right, as you please.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam ukto bhagavatā mahendraḥ pṛthivīṃ tadā cacārairāvataskandham adhiruhya śriyā vṛtaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed by the Blessed One, great Indra then ranged over the earth, mounted upon the shoulder of Airāvata and girt with majesty.

sanskrit: tato dadarśa sa baliṃ kharaveṣeṇa saṃvṛtam yathākhyātaṃ bhagavatā śūnyāgārakṛtālayam
english: Then he beheld Bali, cloaked in the form of an ass, having made his dwelling in an empty house, just as the Blessed One had foretold.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca kharayonim anuprāptas tuṣabhakṣo 'si dānava iyaṃ te yonir adhamā śocasy āho na śocasi
english: Śakra said: Fallen into the womb of an ass, you feed now on chaff, O Dānava. This birth of yours is the lowest — do you grieve, or do you not grieve?

sanskrit: adṛṣṭaṃ bata paśyāmi dviṣatāṃ vaśam āgatam śriyā vihīnaṃ mitraiś ca bhraṣṭavīryaparākramam
english: What never was seen, that, alas, I now behold: you come under the power of your foes, bereft of fortune and of friends, your might and valour fallen away.

sanskrit: yat tad yānasahasreṇa jñātibhiḥ parivāritaḥ lokān pratāpayan sarvān yāsy asmān avitarkayan
english: Once, surrounded by your kinsmen with a thousand chariots, you would go scorching all the worlds, holding us as nothing.

sanskrit: tvanmukhāś caiva daiteyā vyatiṣṭhaṃs tava śāsane akṛṣṭapacyā pṛthivī tavaiśvarye babhūva ha idaṃ ca te 'dya vyasanaṃ śocasy āho na śocasi
english: With you at their head, the Daityas stood obedient to your command, and under your sovereignty the earth yielded harvests untilled. And now this calamity is yours — do you grieve, or do you not grieve?

sanskrit: yadātiṣṭhaḥ samudrasya pūrvakūle vilelihan jñātibhyo vibhajan vittaṃ tadāsīt te manaḥ katham
english: When you stood upon the eastern shore of the ocean, licking your lips as you distributed wealth to your kinsmen — how then was your mind?

sanskrit: yat te sahasrasamitā nanṛtur devayoṣitaḥ bahūni varṣapūgāni vihāre dīpyataḥ śriyā
english: When women of the gods, gathered in their thousands, danced for you through many a span of years in your pleasure-garden, you blazing with splendour —

sanskrit: sarvāḥ puṣkaramālinyaḥ sarvāḥ kāñcanasaprabhāḥ katham adya tadā caiva manas te dānaveśvara
english: all of them garlanded with lotuses, all of them gleaming like gold — how is your mind now and how was it then, O lord of the Dānavas?

sanskrit: chatraṃ tavāsīt sumahat sauvarṇaṃ maṇibhūṣitam nanṛtur yatra gandharvāḥ ṣaṭsahasrāṇi saptadhā
english: Yours was a great parasol of gold, adorned with gems, beneath which the gandharvas danced, six thousand of them in seven bands.

sanskrit: yūpas tavāsīt sumahān yajataḥ sarvakāñcanaḥ yatrādadaḥ sahasrāṇām ayutāni gavāṃ daśa
english: Yours, as you sacrificed, was a vast sacrificial post all of gold, where you gave away ten myriads of thousands of cattle.

sanskrit: yadā tu pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ yajamāno 'nuparyayāḥ śamyākṣepeṇa vidhinā tadāsīt kiṃ nu te hṛdi
english: And when, as sacrificer, you ranged over the whole earth by the rite of casting the yoke-pin — what then was in your heart?

sanskrit: na te paśyāmi bhṛṅgāraṃ na chatraṃ vyajanaṃ na ca brahmadattāṃ ca te mālāṃ na paśyāmy asurādhipa
english: I do not see your golden vessel, nor your parasol, nor your fan; nor do I see the garland given you by Brahmā, O sovereign of the Asuras.

sanskrit: balir uvāca na tvaṃ paśyasi bhṛṅgāraṃ na chatraṃ vyajanaṃ na ca brahmadattāṃ ca me mālāṃ na tvaṃ drakṣyasi vāsava
english: Bali said: You do not see my golden vessel, nor my parasol, nor my fan; nor shall you see the garland given me by Brahmā, O Vāsava.

sanskrit: guhāyāṃ nihitāni tvaṃ mama ratnāni pṛcchasi yadā me bhavitā kālas tadā tvaṃ tāni drakṣyasi
english: You ask after my jewels, but they are laid away in a hidden cavern; when my time shall come again, then you shall behold them.
